summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Experienced in on-device model deployment and inference runtime optimization, having reduced GPU memory footprint by 55% through 8-bit quantization on a 1.1B parameter language model and achieved a 5.2x speedup optimizing TensorRT based model runtimes on Jetson edge hardware. Exported and deployed CNN models to TFLite and ONNX for mobile inference, and built custom CUDA kernels to accelerate model execution at the kernel level.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 images, achieving 83% mAP@50; exported to ONNX and TFLite for mobile deployment.
Curated and annotated a custom toothbrush detection dataset for health-level classification using YOLOv8.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Improved validation accuracy from 55% to 93% via improved preprocessing and model tuning.
Built PyTorch training pipelines using HuggingFace VisionEncoderDecoder; added custom special tokens.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Trained U-Net segmentation (VGG-16/19, ResNet-50); evaluated Dice/IoU and accuracy-latency trade-offs.
Led a cross-cultural team of 7 as sole ML-experienced student, restructuring delivery within a 6-week window.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing: 5.2x speedup (56.7→10.9 ms, 92 FPS) on Jetson.
Built a Flutter mobile client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller over WebSocket.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory ~55% via 8-bit quantization (LLM.int8) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled VRAM/latency with pynvml.
Benchmarked on HellaSwag, GSM8K, ARC: <1% accuracy loss, near-lossless compression.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Coalesced CUDA kernel: 49.2ms vs 73.3ms uncoalesced, 77.5ms CPU TorchScript — ~35% speedup.
Replaced TorchScript conv layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing.
